method: Exact chance enumeration and adversarial two-player backward induction in synthetic final-epoch puzzles. Standard 180-tile conservation and prior/current epoch Ra counts are respected: 15 physical bag tiles (13-14 Ra plus 1-2 non-Ra). Known equal public initial scores 100, 1-2 usable disks per player, all canonical legal actions. Draw probabilities use the public remaining multiset; no future-order peeking. Each objective is solved separately, with a 100000-node cap; capped cases excluded from exact conclusions.
caveats: Synthetic fully specified two-player endgames, not full-game Ra playing-strength evidence.
Deck and Ra-counter constraints are checked, but full reachability from a standard game's complete history is not proven.
Opponent scores are deliberately public and equal in these fixtures; no real hidden score is used.
Policy regret is relative to the stated win or margin objective, not proof of an error in historical games.
The current MCTS itself is not benchmarked here; its restricted candidate set and heuristic policy are audited.
Only two retained fixtures restrict candidates and none exercise god exchanges; the pruning check has narrow coverage.
